sections.name: File setup, esc, n
sections.title: Purpose, imports and text helpers
sections.what: Describes the one-page methodology note and what it draws on. Loads the browser library, the shell command helper, the source policy and the coverage summary. Defines a helper that makes text safe for HTML and a helper that formats numbers with thousands separators.
sections.why: Likely reason: the note is built as HTML, so any text from the data must be escaped to avoid breaking the page.
sections.watch_out: The escape helper covers only ampersands, angle brackets and double quotes, so any other special text is not escaped.

sections.name: methodologyHtml
sections.title: Building the methodology note page
sections.what: Builds the HTML page for the methodology note. It shows the scope and run, the seven-step summary of how the run worked, a table of discrimination scores for each pillar, the coverage ledger of what was used and shown, the source policy with each source's tier, and any qualifications. Coverage data is read from storage when the page is built.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. The note exists so a reader can check how the conclusions were reached.
sections.watch_out: Several sentences and the 0.30 discrimination threshold are typed directly into the text, so any change to the scoring rules must also be made by hand here.

sections.name: methodologyPdf
sections.title: Printing the note to PDF
sections.what: Turns the HTML note into a PDF file in A4 size with background colours kept. It first looks for a system copy of chromium, then starts a headless browser, prints the page and closes the browser, even if printing fails.
sections.why: Likely reason: a real browser prints the page so its layout matches what a reader would see. Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: If no chromium program is found, the browser library falls back to its own default, which may not be installed on the machine.

summary: Makes a one-page A4 PDF methodology note for a Lessons Learnt run, using the saved results and the coverage ledger. Only the setup section was in the packet, so the rest of the file could not be checked.
purpose: Give readers a short printed account of how the run was done, what sources it used, and how outcomes and cells were scored.
why: The header says the note is drawn only from the saved result and ledger, so it does not run new analysis. The reason for producing a PDF is not stated in the code.
how: Per the file header: reads the saved run result and the coverage counts, builds an HTML page of the methodology, and renders that page to PDF with a headless Chromium browser. Only the setup section was visible, so the HTML and rendering steps are from the header and imports, not from the code itself.
inputs: A saved run result and the coverage ledger counts for one run.
risks: Needs a headless browser and a shell command to be available on the server. Page content comes from saved data, so an out-of-date result shows old figures.
debug: If the PDF fails, check that the browser component is installed on the server and that the shell command import can run. If counts look empty, check the coverage summary for that run.
